name: First Pan-African Conference
summary: Three-day conference at Westminster Town Hall, 23–25 July 1900, convened by Henry Sylvester Williams's African Association; it founded the Pan-African Association and adopted the "Address to the Nations of the World".

name: First Universal Races Congress
summary: International congress on relations between "so-called white and so-called coloured peoples", held at the University of London on 26–29 July 1911; W. E. B. Du Bois was a United States secretary and gave a paper on the Negro race in America.

name: Second Pan-African Congress (London Session)
summary: The London sessions of the Second Pan-African Congress, held at Central Hall, Westminster, in late August 1921, before sessions in Brussels and Paris; convened by W. E. B. Du Bois, they adopted the outspoken "London Manifesto".

name: Fifth Pan-African Congress (Manchester)
summary: The Pan-African Congress held at Chorlton Town Hall, Manchester, in October 1945, organised by the Pan-African Federation, with W. E. B. Du Bois as International President; its declarations demanded colonial independence.

name: Nelson Mandela's Clandestine Visit
summary: Nelson Mandela's secret ten-day stay in London in June 1962, during his tour of Africa to win support for the ANC's armed struggle, when he saw Oliver Tambo and met British politicians.

name: Address in Westminster Hall
summary: Nelson Mandela's address as President of South Africa to both Houses of Parliament assembled in Westminster Hall on 11 July 1996.

name: Visit to Brixton
summary: Nelson Mandela's visit to Brixton, south London, in 1996, remembered by residents and recalled in the Commons tributes of 2013.

name: Baptism of Gustavus Vassa
summary: The baptism of the boy then called Gustavus Vassa, later known as Olaudah Equiano, at St Margaret's Church, Westminster, on 9 February 1759, with Miss Guerin as godmother.

name: Westminster Parliamentary Elections
summary: The Westminster parliamentary elections of 1774 and 1780, in which the grocer and writer Ignatius Sancho voted as a male householder.

name: Court of Common Pleas Trial (Pringle v. Cadell)
summary: Thomas Pringle's libel action against the London publisher Thomas Cadell, heard in the Court of Common Pleas on 21 February 1833, at which Mary Prince briefly gave evidence.

name: Court of King's Bench Trial (Wood v. Pringle)
summary: John Adams Wood's libel action against Thomas Pringle, heard in the Court of King's Bench on 27 February 1833, at which Mary Prince was the first defence witness and gave a detailed account of her life.

name: National Chartist Convention & Kennington Demo
summary: The National Chartist Convention, which assembled in London on 4 April 1848, and the mass meeting on Kennington Common on 10 April, whose processions William Cuffay's Demonstration Committee organised.

name: Police Raid on Orange Tree Public House
summary: The police raid of 16 August 1848 on the "Ulterior Committee" of Chartists and Irish Confederates meeting at the Orange Tree public house near Holborn, which ended a planned rising; William Cuffay, its secretary, was arrested two days later.

name: Old Bailey trial of William Cuffay et al. (September 1848 session)
summary: The trial of William Cuffay, William Lacey and Thomas Fay at the Central Criminal Court in the September 1848 session, for feloniously compassing to levy war against the Queen; Cuffay was convicted and transported for life.

name: Premiere of Hiawatha's Wedding Feast
summary: The first performance of Samuel Coleridge-Taylor's cantata Hiawatha's Wedding Feast, at a Royal College of Music concert conducted by Sir Charles Stanford on 11 November 1898.

name: Founding of WASU
summary: The meeting of West African students in London in August 1925 at which, after a heated debate, the West African Students' Union was founded, with J. B. Danquah as president and Ladipo Solanke as secretary-general.

name: Founding Meeting of LCP
summary: The meeting at the Central YMCA, Tottenham Court Road, on 13 March 1931 at which Dr Harold Moody and his supporters founded the League of Coloured Peoples.

name: Staging of Toussaint Louverture
summary: The Stage Society's production of C. L. R. James's play Toussaint Louverture at the Westminster Theatre in March 1936, with Paul Robeson in the title role.

name: Caribbean Carnival
summary: The first Caribbean Carnival organised by the West Indian Gazette, held indoors at St Pancras Town Hall on Friday 30 January 1959 and partly televised by the BBC, in response to the 1958 riots.

name: Othello at the Savoy Theatre (opening night)
summary: The opening night, 19 May 1930, of Maurice Browne's production of Othello at the Savoy Theatre, London, with Paul Robeson as Othello and Peggy Ashcroft as Desdemona.

name: ANC Office Bombing
summary: The bombing of the African National Congress's London headquarters at 28 Penton Street, Islington, on the morning of Sunday 14 March 1982, by agents of the South African security services.

name: International Book Fair of Radical Black and Third World Books (first fair)
summary: The first International Book Fair of Radical Black and Third World Books, a week-long festival at Islington Town Hall in April 1982, planned by John La Rose, Jessica and Eric Huntley and others from January 1981.

name: Black People's Day of Action
summary: The Black People's Day of Action of Monday 2 March 1981, a national march through London called by the New Cross Massacre Action Committee to protest at the official and press response to the New Cross fire.

name: Mangrove Demo
summary: The march of Sunday 9 August 1970 from the Mangrove restaurant in All Saints Road, Notting Hill, to protest at repeated police raids on the restaurant, organised by the Action Committee for Defence of the Mangrove with the Black Panther Movement.

name: Mangrove Nine Trial
summary: The trial of the Mangrove Nine at the Old Bailey, from 5 October to mid-December 1971, at which all nine were acquitted of incitement to riot and the judge acknowledged "evidence of racial hatred on both sides".

name: Clement Gomwalk Incident
summary: The arrest of the Nigerian diplomat Clement Gomwalk by police in Brixton on 15 November 1969, in which the seventeen-year-old Olive Morris intervened and was arrested and, by her own account, beaten.
